# Proposed not-applicable OWASP requirements: engineering report

*Generated by `tools/security/na_report.py` from `tests/security/coverage.json` and `tests/security/na-categories.json`; do not edit by hand.*

Of the 442 pinned OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 and WSTG 4.2 requirements, **320** are proposed as not applicable to CYBOU, a desktop browser that serves nothing, holds no accounts and has no back end. This report gives the ground for each proposal, the architecture it rests on, the browser risks that are still tested in its place, and when it must be reconsidered.

It is an engineering report, not an approval. The rows stay `untriaged` proposals; item-by-item review by a named reviewer is a 1.0.0-rc gate ([VERSIONING](VERSIONING.md)).

## How the grounds are kept honest

Each category names **architecture facts**: patterns the product sources must not contain. The facts are checked against 61 product files under `src/` and `qml/` (test fixtures and diagnostic probes excluded, since they are built only into `cybou_tests`). `owasp_gate.py --mode framework` runs the same check, so a change that breaks a fact fails the gate and reopens every category resting on it.

| Fact | Claim | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `no-server` | The product opens no listening socket: no TCP, UDP, local or HTTP/WebSocket server. | holds |
| `no-own-http-client` | All network traffic is page traffic made by the engine; the product sends no requests of its own (no telemetry, back end or log upload). | holds |
| `no-credential-storage` | The product stores no password, secret or token of its own; credentials met in URLs are stripped or refused. | holds |
| `no-oauth-client` | The product is not an OAuth/OIDC client or server: it never requests, exchanges or stores grants. | holds |
| `no-token-handling` | The product neither issues nor parses self-contained tokens. | holds |
| `no-session-issuance` | The product sets no cookies and issues no sessions; it only filters the engine's cookie store. | holds |
| `no-own-crypto` | The product has no cryptography, hashing or random generation of its own; all of it is the engine's. | holds |
| `no-query-languages` | The product builds no SQL, LDAP, XPath, XML, template or script from data; it embeds no script engine of its own. | holds |
| `no-dynamic-regex` | Every regular expression is a fixed literal; no user or page input is compiled into one. | holds |
| `no-media-server` | The product configures no STUN/TURN server and relays no media; WebRTC is the engine's endpoint only. | holds |
| `no-archive-extraction` | The product unpacks no archive and processes no uploaded file on behalf of others. | holds |
| `no-secret-env` | The product reads no secret from the environment; the only variable read is the engine flag list. | holds |
| `no-log-sink` | The product installs no log handler and writes no log to a system or remote sink. | holds |
| `no-thread-pool` | The product runs no worker pool of its own that requests could starve. | holds |

## WSTG scenarios for testing a web application (72)

WSTG tests a server application through a browser: fingerprinting it, probing its configuration, accounts, sessions and input handling. CYBOU is the client in that picture and serves nothing, so these scenarios have no target. The WSTG scenarios with a browser-side counterpart (client-side, transport, redirects) are already applicable.

**Rests on:** `no-server` (holds); `no-own-http-client` (holds)

**Architecture:** [ARCHITECTURE_OVERVIEW.md](../docs/ARCHITECTURE_OVERVIEW.md), [NavigationGuard.h](../src/security/NavigationGuard.h), [RequestObserver.h](../src/controlbar/RequestObserver.h)

**Browser risks still tested:** CYB-HTTP-001 (strict HTTPS, downgrade and SSL errors); CYB-HTTP-002 (HTTP consent exact address, redirects, first party resources and ws); CYB-ORIGIN-001 (real cross-origin fetch CORS preflight, credential isolation and reje…); CYB-INPUT-002 (navigation guard spoofed origin, redirect chain and homographs)

**Reconsider when:** CYBOU ships a web service or a local web UI (an update server, a sync service, a settings page served over HTTP).

<a id="authentication"></a>

## Authentication of users of a service (47)

These controls govern how a service verifies its users. CYBOU has no accounts, no login of its own and no password manager; sign-in to cloud services happens on the providers' own pages inside ordinary tabs. The browser-side duty is not to leak or mishandle credentials, which is covered by URL credential stripping and the logging cases.

**Rests on:** `no-credential-storage` (holds); `no-server` (holds); `no-oauth-client` (holds)

**Architecture:** [NetworkPolicy.h](../src/security/NetworkPolicy.h), [StoredUrl.h](../src/security/StoredUrl.h), [0007-selectable-cloud-services.md](../docs/ADR/0007-selectable-cloud-services.md)

**Browser risks still tested:** CYB-LOG-001 (no credentials cookies tokens or document content in logs); CYB-CLOUD-004 (real login 2FA and file workflows on each vendor WebEngine); CYB-SBX-002 (cookies storage private/profile boundaries and crash recovery)

**Reconsider when:** CYBOU adds accounts, sync, a password or passkey manager, or any sign-in of its own.

<a id="oauth-oidc"></a>

## OAuth and OpenID Connect roles (36)

Each control targets a client, an authorization server, a resource server or an OpenID Provider. CYBOU plays none of these roles; it only carries the redirects as a user agent. What the user agent owes the flow (no token leakage into stored history, correct redirect handling) is covered elsewhere.

**Rests on:** `no-oauth-client` (holds); `no-token-handling` (holds)

**Architecture:** [StoredUrl.h](../src/security/StoredUrl.h), [NavigationGuard.h](../src/security/NavigationGuard.h)

**Browser risks still tested:** CYB-HTTP-002 (HTTP consent exact address, redirects, first party resources and ws); CYB-INPUT-002 (navigation guard spoofed origin, redirect chain and homographs); CYB-LOG-002 (diagnostics cannot leak browsing history without opt in)

**Reconsider when:** CYBOU itself signs in to a provider (sync, cloud API access) or keeps tokens on the user's behalf.

<a id="web-headers"></a>

## Response headers, cookies and hosting practices (26)

These controls ask a site to send security headers, set cookie attributes and host content safely. A browser does not send them; it enforces them. Enforcement belongs to the engine and is exercised by the transport, origin and redirect cases.

**Rests on:** `no-server` (holds); `no-session-issuance` (holds)

**Reconsider when:** CYBOU serves any page (local web UI, internal scheme with its own headers) or sets cookies itself.

**Browser risks still tested:** CYB-PERM-003 (stale ID / pending queue cancellation / revoke all fail closed)

**Reconsider when:** CYBOU issues or accepts a token, including one exposed to page content.

<a id="backend-coding"></a>

## Back-end coding practices (7)

Mass assignment, proxy headers, parameter pollution and request-thread starvation are server patterns. CYBOU binds no request data to objects, sits behind no proxy and runs no worker pool of its own; its JavaScript is the engine's.

**Rests on:** `no-server` (holds); `no-thread-pool` (holds)

**Architecture:** [ARCHITECTURE_OVERVIEW.md](../docs/ARCHITECTURE_OVERVIEW.md)

**Browser risks still tested:** CYB-FAIL-002 (randomized stress 100 tabs and high rate permission requests); CYB-FUZZ-002 (fuzz cloud QSettings JSON and provider catalog input)

**Reconsider when:** CYBOU adds a server, a worker pool or binds external data to its objects.

<a id="server-files"></a>

## Server-side upload and archive processing (5)

Upload quotas and archive extraction apply to services receiving files from many users. CYBOU unpacks nothing; its own file intake (downloads, wallpaper) is covered by the applicable file controls, and local disk exhaustion by CYB-FAIL-001.

**Rests on:** `no-archive-extraction` (holds); `no-server` (holds)

**Architecture:** [DownloadPolicy.h](../src/security/DownloadPolicy.h)

**Browser risks still tested:** CYB-INPUT-003 (safe PDF/download path traversal execution and filename sanitization); CYB-FAIL-001 (unexpected shutdown disk full interrupted download and low memory)

**Reconsider when:** CYBOU extracts archives, imports files from another program, or receives files from other parties.

<a id="server-caching"></a>

## Server-side caching and data exposure (5)

These controls cover what a server caches and returns. CYBOU returns nothing to anyone; the data it keeps locally (history, bookmarks, profiles) is covered by the applicable data-protection controls.

**Rests on:** `no-server` (holds); `no-own-http-client` (holds)

**Architecture:** [browserstore.h](../src/browserstore.h), [DATA_CLASSIFICATION.md](../docs/DATA_CLASSIFICATION.md)

**Browser risks still tested:** CYB-SBX-002 (cookies storage private/profile boundaries and crash recovery); CYB-LOG-002 (diagnostics cannot leak browsing history without opt in)

**Reconsider when:** CYBOU sends or serves its local data (sync, export to a service).

<a id="tls-server"></a>

## TLS server and service-to-service transport (4)

CYBOU terminates no TLS and calls no back-end service. As a TLS client it is covered by the strict HTTPS and certificate controls.

**Rests on:** `no-server` (holds); `no-own-http-client` (holds)

**Architecture:** [NavigationGuard.h](../src/security/NavigationGuard.h), [TlsBoundaryTests.h](../src/security/TlsBoundaryTests.h)

**Browser risks still tested:** CYB-HTTP-001 (strict HTTPS, downgrade and SSL errors)

**Reconsider when:** The update repository or any CYBOU service goes public (ASVS 12.2.2 first).

<a id="log-pipelines"></a>

## Central log pipelines and log transmission (4)

Shipping logs to a separate system protects a breached server's audit trail. A private local browser deliberately keeps diagnostics on the machine and authenticates nobody, so there is nothing to ship; what it may record locally is covered by the logging cases.

**Rests on:** `no-log-sink` (holds); `no-own-http-client` (holds)

**Architecture:** [DATA_CLASSIFICATION.md](../docs/DATA_CLASSIFICATION.md), [minidump_summary.py](../tools/security/minidump_summary.py)

**Browser risks still tested:** CYB-LOG-001 (no credentials cookies tokens or document content in logs); CYB-LOG-002 (diagnostics cannot leak browsing history without opt in)

**Reconsider when:** CYBOU adds crash reporting, telemetry or any upload of diagnostics.
